# 📝 Notes

Jun 10, 2026

## Chameleon Profile Page Discussion

Invited [Austin Dillman](mailto:austin@chameleon.co) [Juan Morales](mailto:juan@chameleon.co) [Chris Baccus](mailto:chris.baccus@chameleon.co) [Jeff Blettner](mailto:jeff.blettner@chameleon.co) [Pamela Alegria](mailto:pamela.alegria@chameleon.co)

Attachments [Chameleon Profile Page Discussion](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/event?eid=N21pZmlyYW05ODcycTM3aGRkaDU3Y3ZrdDkgYXVzdGluQGNoYW1lbGVvbi5jbw)

Meeting records [Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19gjESt0Yl2OVjUfC0rvvkVwtD1zz2Dz0ge03eW_L74I/edit?usp=drive_web&tab=t.jtmqb1buoc98) 

### Summary

Committee discussed redesigning profile pages for improved flexibility and integration with Artificial Intelligence tools for client pitching.

**Current profile limitations**  
Existing profile pages are frequently considered unpolished and outdated, leading members to prefer custom slide decks for client pitches. Members demand greater control over content customization and modular layouts to better reflect their specific skills and professional credibility.

**Enhancing platform capabilities**  
The redesign will integrate Artificial Intelligence to dynamically generate tailored bios and automated content for job applications. Participants prioritized the ability to curate testimonials and display client experience while maintaining consistent branding across the collective.

**Strategic project implementation**  
The team agreed to provide both web-based profiles and downloadable formats to streamline group pitching processes. A 6-week timeline was established to finalize wireframes and design components for the new platform.

### Decisions

## Aligned

* **Chameleon profile page redesign project** The growth committee will undertake a six-week project to redesign Chameleon profile pages, culminating in a hand-off of design wireframes to the core team.

* **Automated client testimonial collection system** The platform will implement an automated system to request and collect client testimonials and feedback following project engagements.

We've **updated the Decisions section** using your feedback.

Let us know what you think: [Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5p6FWBVWvynleNU?isGoogler=no&isHelpful=yes) or [Not Helpful](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5p6FWBVWvynleNU?isGoogler=no&isHelpful=no)

### Next steps

- [ ] \[Juan Morales, Austin Dillman, Freddy\] Produce Audiobook: Create an audio version of the published project to increase accessibility and engagement.

- [ ] \[Juan Morales, Austin Dillman\] Rebuild Profile Pages: Implement user feedback to create an editable and polished profile page system for Chameleon members.

- [ ] \[The group\] Create Slack Group: Establish a communication channel to share profile page design outputs with the contributors for feedback.

- [ ] \[The group\] Design Profile Pages: Develop wireframes and visual compositions for the updated profile pages within a 6 week timeframe.

- [ ] \[The group\] Hand Off Designs: Deliver the finalized profile page designs to the core website development team after the 6 week project period.

### Details

*Did the screenshots in this section make your notes [better](https://goo.gle/44IH7J9) or [worse](https://goo.gle/4b5ZWtJ)?*

* **Audiobook Project**: Juan Morales shares that the team is "cooking up" a plan to create an audiobook, which they intend to produce collaboratively between the three of them ([00:01:42](#00:01:42)).

* **Meeting Purpose and Scope**: Juan Morales and Austin Dillman introduce the informal growth committee's project, which aims to redesign Chameleon profile pages hosted on the Chameleon Collective website. The goal is to provide tools that help members get more work and to make it easier for peers to sell each other's services ([00:02:28](#00:02:28)).

  ![][image1]

* **Current State of Profile Pages**: Pamela Alegria, Chris Baccus, and Jeff Blettner provide feedback that current profile pages are often unpolished, outdated, and infrequently used. Participants prefer using custom-made slide decks or personal websites for client pitches because they feel the current profile pages lack the necessary polish and targeted content ([00:04:20](#00:04:20)) ([00:08:10](#00:08:10)).

* **Need for Content Customization**: The group discusses the necessity of customizing bios for specific clients. Austin Dillman, Chris Baccus, and Jeff Blettner agree that because they often need to target specific client restrictions, they frequently edit their profiles outside of Chameleon OS, suggesting that the profile platform should allow for more flexible, tailored editing ([00:10:27](#00:10:27)).

* **Personal Ownership of Content**: Participants express a desire for greater ownership over their profile pages, including the ability to edit content, add case studies, and select from a library of modules. Pamela Alegria and Chris Baccus emphasize that while they maintain personal websites, they would utilize a more robust, customizable Chameleon page if it were available ([00:12:14](#00:12:14)).

* **Skill and Role Definition**: Participants discuss the challenge of managing overly broad skill tags that may appear on profiles. Chris Baccus and Austin Dillman agree that members should focus on highlighting their "superpowers" or most relevant current skills rather than listing every skill from a long career, as this improves credibility and avoids confusing potential clients ([00:15:13](#00:15:13)).

* **Client Lists and Privacy**: The discussion covers how to represent past client experience. Chris Baccus and Austin Dillman note the importance of providing context regarding client size and stage (e.g., Series B, employee count), while acknowledging privacy concerns regarding displaying client logos publicly. They suggest giving individual members the ability to curate which logos are displayed on their specific pages ([00:17:20](#00:17:20)).

* **Profile Format Preferences**: Jeff Blettner and Pamela Alegria express a preference for a more condensed, slide-like format for profiles, similar to Google Slides, which allows for a quick scan of the most important information, such as mini case studies and client logos ([00:20:40](#00:20:40)).

* **Client Decision Criteria**: Jeff Blettner outlines the top three things clients look for: proven results, experience that is communicated succinctly, and personalization. He describes his process of using AI to analyze call notes and refine his profile/proposal to better match client interests, which is not currently supported by Chameleon OS ([00:22:57](#00:22:57)).

* **AI-Driven Personalization**: Juan Morales suggests that the new profile platform could utilize AI to allow members to dynamically generate tailored bios or content for specific job descriptions, acknowledging that members are already using AI workflows to customize their materials ([00:24:19](#00:24:19)).

* **Culture and Credibility**: Pamela Alegria highlights that culture fit is a major decision factor for clients. She notes that current profiles can cause confusion for clients who see a mix of personal websites and inconsistent branding, whereas a unified, credible Chameleon Collective profile page would provide stronger backing ([00:26:27](#00:26:27)).

* **Usage of Video Content**: Juan Morales explores the potential for using video introductions on profiles. Jeff Blettner and Chris Baccus agree that video can effectively showcase personality and culture fit, though they acknowledge that not everyone will be comfortable with this, and usage will likely vary ([00:29:46](#00:29:46)).

* **Testimonials and Social Proof**: The group discusses the lack of formal testimonial collection. Juan Morales and Jeff Blettner discuss the idea of automating testimonial requests after project completion. Participants agree that having a place to display validated testimonials or reviews would add credibility, with Chris Baccus suggesting the ability to moderate which reviews appear ([00:33:37](#00:33:37)) ([00:37:06](#00:37:06)).

* **Lead Generation Strategy**: Juan Morales asks if members would be motivated to create thought leadership content if it resulted in lead generation forms sent directly to them. Chris Baccus and Pamela Alegria express a preference for keeping lead generation centralized rather than individual, to maintain the cohesive branding of Chameleon Collective ([00:38:36](#00:38:36)).

* **Sizzle Reels and Content Freshness**: Austin Dillman raises the idea of using AI to create automated "sizzle reels" of design work to keep portfolios fresh. Pamela Alegria notes that while this is appealing, the process must be easy and reliable to avoid adding a significant workload or creating "cheesy" content ([00:42:49](#00:42:49)).

* **Web Profiles vs. PDF Slides**: The participants debate the value of web-based profiles versus PDF slides. Juan Morales points out that web-based profiles are mobile-responsive and can be auto-updated, while Pamela Alegria and Jeff Blettner note that they currently rely on PDF slides for a more "polished" look. The consensus is that providing both options would be ideal ([00:48:24](#00:48:24)).

* **Group Pitching Process**: Austin Dillman asks how members currently handle situations where they must pitch multiple Chameleon Collective members at once. Participants confirm they currently download PDFs and compile them manually. The group identifies a need to streamline this process so that all profiles are structured cohesively, avoiding the disjointed feeling of sending varied links or disparate documents ([00:51:32](#00:51:32)).

* **Project Timeline**: Juan Morales concludes the meeting by stating that the project will take six weeks. The team aims to produce wireframes and design comps for the new profiles, which will be shared with the group via Slack for feedback before being handed off to the core team for implementation ([00:55:19](#00:55:19)).
